notes.summary: Environment usually gives 1 question: ecosystem basics, pollution and its diseases, global environmental agreements, and India's national parks and wildlife projects.

concepts.title: Ecosystem and food chain
concepts.body:
• Producers (green plants) make food by photosynthesis; consumers eat others; decomposers (bacteria, fungi) break down dead matter.
  • Energy flows in one direction: Sun → producers → herbivores → carnivores.
  • 10% law (Lindeman): only about 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level; the rest is lost mostly as heat. So food chains are short.
  • An energy pyramid is always upright.

concepts.title: Pollution and global agreements
concepts.body:
• Greenhouse gases: carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, water vapour, CFCs.
  • Ozone depletion is caused mainly by CFCs.
  • Acid rain: sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides.

concepts.title: Protected areas and wildlife projects
concepts.body:
PlaceKnown for
Jim Corbett NP (Uttarakhand)India's first national park, 1936 (as Hailey NP)
Kaziranga NP (Assam)One-horned rhinoceros
Gir NP (Gujarat)Asiatic lion — Gir region is its only wild home
Sundarbans (West Bengal)Mangroves, Royal Bengal tiger
Silent Valley (Kerala)Tropical evergreen forest, lion-tailed macaque
  • Project Tiger: 1973. Project Elephant: 1992.
  • Wildlife (Protection) Act: 1972. Environment (Protection) Act: 1986, passed after the Bhopal gas tragedy (1984, methyl isocyanate).
  • Chipko Movement (1973, Uttarakhand): people hugged trees to stop felling; linked with Sunderlal Bahuguna.
  • India has parts of 4 biodiversity hotspots: Himalaya, Western Ghats–Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, Sundaland.

example.q: Kaziranga National Park is famous for:

tips: Agreements in year order: Ramsar 1971 → Montreal 1987 → Rio 1992 → Kyoto 1997 → Paris 2015.
Gir = lions, Kaziranga = rhinos, Sundarbans = tigers in mangroves.
traps: Montreal is about ozone; Kyoto and Paris are about climate (greenhouse gases).
The energy pyramid is always upright; a pyramid of numbers or biomass may be inverted.
Jim Corbett, not Kaziranga, was India's first national park.

questions.q: Gir National Park is famous for which animal?
questions.solution:
Gir National Park and the surrounding Gir forest region of Gujarat form the only wild home of the Asiatic lion.
Memory hook: Gir — 'Gir-r-r' is the lion's roar.

questions.q: In an ecosystem, green plants are called:
questions.solution:
Green plants make their own food by photosynthesis, so they are producers.
Memory hook: Plants Produce.

questions.q: Which gas is mainly responsible for depletion of the ozone layer?
questions.solution:
CFCs release chlorine in the stratosphere, which breaks down ozone. They were used in fridges and sprays.
Memory hook: Chlorine from CFCs 'chews' ozone.

questions.q: Minamata disease is caused by poisoning from:
questions.solution:
Minamata disease (Japan) was caused by mercury in fish from polluted water. Itai-itai is due to cadmium.
Memory hook: Minamata = Mercury.

questions.q: Which was the first national park of India?
questions.solution:
Jim Corbett National Park (Uttarakhand) was set up in 1936 as Hailey National Park — India's first. Project Tiger was launched here in 1973.
Memory hook: Corbett: first park, first Project Tiger reserve.

questions.q: According to Lindeman's 10% law, if producers trap 20,000 J of energy, how much will reach the secondary consumers?
questions.solution:
Primary consumers get 10% of 20,000 = 2,000 J. Secondary consumers get 10% of 2,000 = 200 J.
Memory hook: Drop one zero at each step up the pyramid.

questions.q: Which international agreement is specifically aimed at protecting the ozone layer?
questions.solution:
The Montreal Protocol (1987) phases out ozone-depleting substances such as CFCs. Kyoto and Paris deal with greenhouse gases; Ramsar with wetlands.
Memory hook: 'O' in Ozone — the 'O' in mOntreal.

questions.q: The Environment (Protection) Act of India was passed in 1986 after which disaster?
questions.solution:
The Bhopal gas tragedy (December 1984, methyl isocyanate leak from Union Carbide) led to the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
Memory hook: Bhopal '84 → Act '86.
